properties.Location: South Side of Santa Rosa Island, Between Ford Point and South Point
properties.IncidentOverview: Current Situation – May 20; 2026 Monday night the Santa Rosa Island Fire remained active once again primarily on the eastern half of the fire; specifically the areas along the Main (Soledad) Road and Telephone Road; south of Black Mountain. Firefighters were able to go direct and build containment line along the Telephone Road in the direction of Cherry Canyon. The fire was also active southwest of Black Rock; upslope from East Point Road as it gradually consumes unburned vegetation. Additionally; activity was observed downslope and southeast of Soledad Peak near Quinn Knob Road. Today; more firefighters and equipment will arrive on the island; including a crew from Chumash Fire Department who have a special connection to Channel Islands National Park as Chumash Homelands. The U.S. Wildland Fire Service has also sent National Park Service firefighting resource advisors to the island who will be working in tandem with the Chumash to protect cultural and natural resources. Fire equipment includes specially designed wildland fire engines; smaller than normal city fire engines; which means they can access additional areas across the island and use existing non-paved dirt roads. Known as type-6 engines; they were loaded on the National Park Service’s landing craft yesterday evening and are enroute this morning. Firefighters will continue working on enhancing defensible space preparation of the structures in the Main Ranch Complex ahead of and if the main fire front reaches that area. For aircraft today; the unmanned aircraft system (UAS) module will be focusing on the Torrey Pines area and doing an assessment of conditions as they make their way to that part of the fire. Fire observation aircraft will be flying this morning to coordinate with the firefighters on the ground to look for opportunities to use fixed wing air tankers such as water scoopers that can drop 1;500 gallons of water at a time. Background: On Friday; May 15; 2026; an aircraft flying over Santa Rosa Island in Channel Islands National Park reported a wildfire. National Park Service (NPS) staff already on the island confirmed it later that morning. The Santa Rosa Island Fire is located on the southeastern end of the island in remote and rugged terrain. This is a full-suppression human-caused wildfire and is under investigation. Closures: The National Park Service has closed Santa Rosa Island to day use and overnight use at least through this week due to the wildfire. Visitors with campground reservations at Water Canyon Campground have been notified via e-mail. Structures: There are two uninhabited historic structures in the area; Johnson’s Lee Equipment Shed on the western edge; and Wreck Line Camp Cabin on the eastern edge. Unfortunately; both have been confirmed destroyed. An additional storage structure was also destroyed adjacent to Johnson’s Lee Equipment Shed.
